core_obligations: Reduce to the case of a proper curve over k using the description of the degree in terms of the components and elementary arithmetic (proof lines 9812-9813).
Choose a modification f : X' -> X such that f^*E admits a filtration with invertible successive quotients, and use the birational invariance of the degree to replace X by X' (proof lines 9814-9818).

Given the filtration 0 = E_0 subset ... subset E_n = E with invertible quotients L_i, compute det(E) = L_1 tensor ... tensor L_n by the determinant of a short exact sequence and induction (proof lines 9819-9827).
Conclude the equality of degrees from multiplicativity of the degree under tensor product and additivity of the degree along the filtration (proof lines 9828-9829).
proof_roadmap: Pass to a modification making the bundle filtrable by invertible quotients.
Compute the determinant inductively from the filtration.
Apply multiplicativity and additivity of the degree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves deg(E) = deg(det(E)) = deg(Lambda^n E) for a locally free module of rank n on a proper scheme of dimension at most one. The proof reduces to the case of a proper curve using the componentwise description of the degree and elementary arithmetic, then uses a modification f : X' -> X after which f^*E admits a filtration with invertible quotients, and the birational-invariance of the degree to work on X' (proof lines 9812-9818). There the determinant is computed inductively as the tensor product of the invertible quotients by the determinant of a short exact sequence, and the claim follows from multiplicativity of the degree and additivity with respect to the filtration (proof lines 9819-9829). H2: the reduction to the filtered case through a modification together with the inductive determinant computation is the substance.
